# Agent Compatibility and Integration Patterns

Dimension covering how OpenShell wraps agents, credential handling, privacy
routing, SDK requirements, and the "agent agnostic" claim.

## Supported Agents

| Agent | Default Policy Coverage | Notes |
|-------|------------------------|-------|
| Claude Code | Full | Works out-of-box [4] |
| OpenCode | Partial | Requires additional endpoint configuration [4] |
| Codex | None | Requires custom policy [4] |
| Cursor | Listed as supported [8] | Default policy coverage not specified |
| OpenClaw | Listed as supported [8] | Default policy coverage not specified |

"If you run a non-Claude agent without a custom policy, the agent's API calls
are denied by the proxy" [4].

## Zero-Code-Change Claim

The NVIDIA blog states: "OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode — zero
code modifications required" [8]. This is technically true — no agent source
code changes needed. However, the default policy documentation directly
contradicts uniform out-of-box support [4].

The "zero code modifications" claim is valid at the agent binary level but
obscures significant configuration requirements for non-Claude agents.

## Deployment Mechanism

```bash
openshell sandbox create --policy ./my-policy.yaml -- claude
# or with remote gateway:
openshell sandbox create --remote spark --from openclaw
```
[5][8]

No SDK integration required — OpenShell operates at the infrastructure layer
(containers, sandboxes, network policies) rather than requiring library
changes [8].

## Credential Auto-Discovery

The privacy router handles credential management via the `inference.local`
endpoint [7]:

1. "Strips original credentials from sandbox requests" [7]
2. "Injects configured backend credentials before forwarding to managed model
   endpoint" [7]
3. "Sandboxes don't need their own API keys" [7]

**Constraint**: "Single provider-model pairing per gateway, applies to all
sandboxes" [7]. This means all sandboxes on one gateway route to the same
model provider.

## Privacy Router

"Manages data flow based on cost and privacy policies — not agent preferences"
[8]. "Maintains sensitive context on-device using local open models (like
Nemotron) and routes to frontier models (Claude, GPT) only when policy permits.
Model-agnostic by design" [8].

Cisco adds: "Privacy router keeps sensitive data local, anonymizes cloud-bound
prompts" [17].

### Supported Providers

| Provider Type | API Patterns Supported |
|--------------|----------------------|
| NVIDIA | Not specified [7] |
| OpenAI-compatible | POST /v1/chat/completions, POST /v1/completions, GET /v1/models [7] |
| Anthropic-compatible | POST /v1/messages [7] |

"Requests not matching configured provider's patterns are denied" [7].

Hot-refresh: "credential and inference updates propagate within ~5 seconds
without sandbox recreation" [7].

## "Agent Agnostic" Claim Assessment

The Futurum analyst characterizes OpenShell as a "universal governance wrapper"
that wraps "competitors' agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode)" — a
"structural market advantage masked by open licensing" [20].

The claim is architecturally valid — OpenShell enforces at the OS level and
does not depend on agent internals. It is operationally limited by the default
policy gap: Claude Code is the only agent with full out-of-box support [4].

## Gaps and Limitations

- Only Claude Code works fully out-of-box — other agents require policy work [4]
- Single provider-model per gateway limits multi-model workflows [7]
- No documented credential rotation mechanism
- LangChain integration details could not be verified from primary sources
